newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids edge up but demand thins.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids edge up but demand thins.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices, helped by tight stocks and firm crude, mostly edged up Monday, but some remained skeptical current levels could be sustained with extremely thin underlying demand, industry sources said.
"Prompt stocks are relatively tight, but there's no demand and we're heading into a shoulder period," said a cash trader.
In New York Harbor, prompt one percent firmed a quarter to $18.75-19.00 a barrel, traders said.
Early one percent paper quotes were mixed, with October pegged little changed at about $19, while November was up 15-20 cents to the $19.10-19.35 area.
NYH high sulphurs were steady to up slightly, with three percent now notionally straddling $16.75.
At the U.S. Gulf Coast, one percent gained 25 cents to $17.00-25 area, while three percent was still pegged near $17.
While some also noted cheap gas continued to siphon demand from resid, others said utilities, waiting for lower prices to stock up for winter, may be running out of time.
"People have been waiting for prices to go down and they haven't. Utilities will have to buy sooner or later," said one.
New York Power Authority tendered for 300,000 barrels of 0.3 percent high pour for any-October delivery. Fixed-price bids are due Tuesday, Sept 24.
New York city gate swing gas prices climbed a few cents Monday to the $2.10-2.15/mmBtu area versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.00/mmBtu equivalent.
